title: Anthropic reportedly prices IPO at $83 a share, above projected range
content:
Anthropic has reportedly priced its long-awaited IPO at $83 per share, above its initial range of $70 to $78, signaling strong investor appetite for one of the companies at the center of the AI boom, despite market jitters following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which shook confidence in the industry.
At the IPO price, Anthropic is reportedly valued at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, a significant increase from the $965 billion the company reached in May when it raised $65 billion in its last private market round, but below the $2 trillion it was reportedly aiming for several months ago.
Anthropic will begin its life as a public company on Thursday, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT.” A strong first day of trading would signal that investors remain optimistic about AI adoption, despite recent volatility in AI-driven stocks.
The company’s performance is expected to set expectations for private AI companies, including Anthropic’s main rival OpenAI, which was last reportedly valued at $1.25 billion but has yet to announce plans for an IPO.
Although none of Anthropic’s venture capital investors holds more than a 5% stake in the company, the IPO is a massive windfall for its numerous backers. Investors that own approximately 1% of the company reportedly include Sequoia and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt. Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC also holds about a 1% stake in the company, according to a person familiar with the matter. Other backers set to make billions are Iconiq, Menlo Ventures, Coatue, and Sound Ventures, a firm launched by Guy Oseary and actor Ashton Kutcher, and Spark Ventures, the only VC firm known to hold a board seat at the company.
Some of the company’s existing investors, namely Sequoia, Iconiq, Lightspeed, Accel, and Altimeter Capital Management, are so enthusiastic about Anthropic’s future that they were reportedly planning to buy billions of dollars’ worth of the company’s shares in the IPO.
Yet the investors’ holdings in Anthropic pale in comparison to those of the Claude maker’s strategic partners, Amazon, which owns nearly 15% of the company, and Google, which holds almost 14%. A group of major tech companies, including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners, have also agreed to purchase $26 billion worth of non-voting shares through a private placement alongside the IPO.
The company’s seven co-founders, including CEO Dario Amodei, each sold nearly 3.4 million shares in the IPO, according to the S-1 filing, bringing in about $282 million for each.

report.summary: Anthropic reportedly priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its projected range, valuing the Claude maker at $1.5 trillion ahead of its Nasdaq debut.
report.background: Anthropic’s IPO arrives at a volatile moment for the AI sector. The Claude maker has grown rapidly on enterprise demand for generative AI, backed by strategic investors Amazon and Google. In May, it was valued at $965 billion after raising $65 billion in private markets, and it had reportedly sought a $2 trillion valuation. The offering is seen as a bellwether for AI companies seeking public capital. Investor appetite appears strong despite market jitters after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s reported departure, which shook confidence in AI stocks. Anthropic’s debut will also set expectations for rival OpenAI and other private AI labs weighing whether public markets can support their capital-intensive growth.
key_points: Anthropic reportedly priced shares at $83, above the $70–$78 range, implying a $1.5 trillion fully diluted valuation. That is up from $965 billion in May but below the $2 trillion the company reportedly targeted months earlier.

The company begins trading Thursday on Nasdaq under the ticker “ANT.” A strong first day would signal that public investors remain optimistic about AI adoption despite recent volatility in AI-driven stocks.

Strategic partners dominate ownership: Amazon holds nearly 15% and Google almost 14%. A group including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners agreed to buy $26 billion of non-voting shares in a private placement.
Anthropic’s seven co-founders, including CEO Dario Amodei, each sold about 3.4 million shares in the IPO, netting roughly $282 million each, according to the S-1 filing.

Venture backers see a major windfall even though none holds more than a 5% stake. Sequoia, Iconiq, Lightspeed, Accel, and Altimeter reportedly planned to buy billions of dollars of shares in the offering.
report.impact: A successful Anthropic IPO would validate the AI boom in public markets and give private AI labs a clearer path to liquidity. It could strengthen Anthropic’s access to capital for compute, model development, and enterprise expansion, while pressuring OpenAI and others to clarify their public-market strategies. The close ties to Amazon and Google raise questions about governance and strategic influence. For developers, a well-funded Anthropic may mean more competition, faster model releases, and continued investment in Claude’s API and tooling, but also pricing and platform dependence risks. For regular users, the IPO itself changes little day to day, though public scrutiny could increase focus on safety, reliability, and data practices.
report.tools: To follow Anthropic’s technology, watch the Claude API and Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) for connecting models to tools and data. Claude Code is useful for agentic coding workflows. For open-source evaluation and integration, consider promptfoo, LangChain, and LlamaIndex. These tools help developers test prompts, build retrieval pipelines, and compare Claude against other models as the competitive landscape shifts after the IPO.
